summary: The rework and fixes F11-F18 are sound. The hanging pan servo, shoulder-screw pivot in a heat-set insert, horizontal tap pilots, base knock case, pan-stall case and torque_pan are all present and consistent with report.json. All requirements pass with large margins, the sweeps are clear, and every hex-key path is straight. One real fit problem keeps it from passing: the new base cavity has zero vertical clearance around the pan servo, and the catalog's own documented tab-height spread (15.6 to 16.0 mm) would stop the servo from sliding in.

findings.issue: Zero vertical clearance for the slide-in pan servo. The servo bottom sits at servo_floor_z = 10.0 mm, which is exactly the top of the nut plinth, because the cavity box starts at z = servo_floor_z. The tab tops sit exactly on the deck underside (deck_z = tab_z + tab_t). Horizontal CLEAR is 0.5 mm per side, but the vertical stack has none. catalog SG90 note: tab underside is 15.6 mm (baud-dance) to ~16 mm (TowerPro drawings), a 0.4 mm spread. At 16.0 the servo bottom would be 0.4 mm below the plinth top, so it cannot slide in from -Y. At the low end the tab leaves a gap under the deck and the M2 screws pull the tab up, bending it. The insertion check only proves the nominal geometry. FDM bridge sag on the deck underside also lands at the tab seat.
findings.fix: Lower the cavity floor so the servo hangs from the deck on its tabs with a gap above the plinth. For example, start the cavity 1.0 mm below servo_floor_z (or add a vertical CLEAR term to the cavity), keeping the 8 mm tripod-screw tip room. The servo then hangs from the tab tops, as DESIGN.md says, and tolerates 15.6-16.0 mm. Update the tab-seat/tab_z maths and re-run the insertion check.

findings.issue: The 30 N knock at the camera was added to base_fea (F15), but the yoke has only the 5 N pivot load and the stall cases. A sideways 30 N at the tilt axis (29.5 mm above the plate) puts about 0.9 N*m at the wall root. A hand estimate for a bare 30 x 5 mm wall section gives about 7 MPa across layers against the 13 MPa allowable. The gussets should lower this, but it is not proven.
findings.fix: Add a yoke FEA case with a 30 N knock along Y at the tilt axis, and reacted at the pan-horn screws. Or add a cantilever_stress hand check.

findings.issue: Numbers have gone stale after the rework. DESIGN.md says 59.3 g complete and printed masses of base 14.2 g, yoke 12.8 g, bracket 6.0 g; report.json says 67.6 g, with perimeter-aware estimates of 18.0, 16.0 and 7.6 g. Envelopes are also off (yoke 30 x 72.9 x 43.1 in the report, 40.6 high in DESIGN.md).

The two tab-screw pilots sit about 2 mm from the deck slot edge (ring 79% material, as the edge-distance warning shows), leaving about 1.2 mm of thread ligament. The FEA peak (9.1 MPa, pilot at the slot corner) is the highest stress in the project. The pilots start in a bridged deck underside.
findings.fix: Print the base first as a coupon. If the pilots strip, fit M2 heat-set inserts or widen the ledge. Say in DESIGN.md that the pattern forces this edge distance, as the warning asks.

findings.issue: Putting in the pan servo screws is fiddly. They go up from below through 4.8 mm holes in the plinth and 13 mm of air to the tabs, with a 1.5 mm key that must be at least 25 mm long. Overhang on the bracket is 3.5% (roofs of 2-3 mm horizontal holes).
findings.fix: Say in ASSEMBLY that a magnetic or long hex driver and a ball-end key are needed. Check the slice preview of the bracket holes.

findings.issue: The 21T horn bolt circle, thread and hub height are catalog estimates. The SG90 tab-hole and output-offset positions are scaled from a drawing. The pivot gap (0.9) against cam_clear (0.8) leaves 0.1 mm of margin.
findings.fix: Measure the purchased horns and servos before printing the full set. Print the base and the bracket horn plate as test pieces. Hand-check the tilt, and shim or sand the knuckle if it binds.
